findings.title: Scanner baseline never matches on real ubs output — the extra ubs run is pure cost and never clears an existing finding
findings.evidence: Measured on the live tree. In the repo, real ubs appends a permalink holding the HEAD sha and line number to every detail line: 'lint/checks/20-harness-scheduling.py:62  Subprocess call has no bounded timeout — ... (https://github.com/craigvandotcom/agent-compounds/blob/eec40cffc545f023e7952eb64d971fcc9ee5daa4/lint/checks/20-harness-scheduling.py#L62)'. The same file scanned in a non-git scratch dir (what BASE_OUT does, line 616) prints no URL. With 2 or more files ubs prints ABSOLUTE paths: '/home/.../agent-compounds/lint/checks/...' at HEAD vs '/tmp/<scratch>/lint/checks/...' at base. sig_of keeps both the path ($1) and the whole message tail (URL included), so HEAD_SIGS and BASE_SIGS are always disjoint: PRE_COUNT stays 0 and every existing finding still refuses. Cost of the wasted base run: +1.96 s for 1 file, +2.05 s for 2 files, +4.7 s for 33 files, on every close whose HEAD scan has any finding, with 0 matches. The close-gate.test.sh mock ubs (lines 124-170) echoes relative argv paths with no URL, so AC4b passes against a mock contract the real tool does not follow.
findings.fix: Normalise both sides before matching: in sig_of, remove a trailing ' (https://...#L[0-9]+)' from msg, and make loc relative by removing the '$ROOT/' prefix (HEAD) and the '$SCRATCH/' prefix (base). Add a test fixture made from captured real ubs output (absolute path plus permalink), so the mock follows the real contract.

findings.title: Base-tree ubs scan runs even when summary-only findings already make refusal certain
findings.evidence: Summary-only findings (SUM_TOTAL > HEAD_COUNT) are always counted NEW (lines 642-645), so the close refuses whatever the baseline says. The base scan (lines 603-619) still runs first. Measured over lint/checks/*.py (33 files): summary Critical 0 / Warning 6 / Info 179 = 185, but only 25 detail lines, so 160 unmatched findings. That makes refusal certain, yet another 4.7 s ubs run happens before it. Any Python bead with bandit-style Info findings hits this.
findings.fix: Compute SUM_TOTAL and HEAD_COUNT before the BASE_USABLE block. If SUM_TOTAL > HEAD_COUNT, refuse straight away (or skip the base scan) instead of building the scratch tree and running ubs a second time.

findings.title: New label lookup fetches the same bead with br show again, right after br_field did
findings.evidence: Line 185 BEAD_TYPE=$(br_field "$BEAD" issue_type) and line 186 BEAD_LABELS=$(br_call show "$BEAD" --json ...) both run br show on the same bead one after the other. Measured br_call show = 0.047-0.048 s (br show 0.043-0.044 s, 3 runs, 562-row ledger), so +~45 ms on every close, on every path. With this addition the gate calls br show on the same bead at least 6 times per close (lines 185, 186, 362, 690, 691, 726; 235 on the ruling path) = ~270 ms of repeated reads.
findings.fix: Read the bead once: SHOW_JSON=$(br_call show "$BEAD" --json) || not_checked ...; then take issue_type and labels with a single jq call (e.g. jq -r '[.issue_type, ((.labels//[])|join(","))]|@tsv'). Reuse SHOW_JSON for description, status and assignee until the write at line 724 (only the post-write status read needs a fresh fetch).
